summary: Racing HUD window: the layout sub-window embedded at layout+0x210 that owns the pane group named 'racing' and the lap-number panes.
evidence: Ui_RaceWindow_BindPanels (0x004511A8) is called by Ui_Layout_BuildTwoChildren (0x00411588) as Ui_RaceWindow_BindPanels(self+0x210, self+0x98), and the same sub-object is passed to Ui_Racing_InitLapNumberPanes, so the class is the racing HUD window embedded in the race layout. The base constructor is the shared Ui widget constructor 0x001A6520 (seed symbol drN, 273 callers); the exact base class is not resolved. Size 6512 = 0x1970 is only the highest strong field + 4, a lower bound.

fields.name: racingPane
fields.evidence: `self->f_196c = func_0053649C(layoutOwner->f_14, "racing")` - the pane-group lookup by name, the same idiom as Ui_GaugeBar_BindPanes storing the 'gauge_bar' group at gaugeBar+4; the following loop sets bit 0 of +0x44 on every child of the returned group. The same offset is read by Ui_Window_BindChildLayoutBlocks (0x00451058), so it is a layout pane-group pointer, not a scalar.

summary: Phantom class: its only method is a shared two-byte flag builder called from 24 unrelated windows, so no result-window object is proven to exist.
evidence: The single method maybe_Ui_BuildFlags (0x0064055C) has 24 callers from unrelated windows (Ui_DiveWindow, Ui_NumberRoll, Ui_SmithMenu, Ui_SubWindow, Ui_TxtLowerWindow, Ui_ThreeLineTwoSelectWindow) and its body only fills a two-byte flag pair from one byte of its first argument; refine pass R2_013 already rejected the 'ResultWindow_BuildEntryFlags' name. The generated class name is kept, but the object is not proven. Size 288 = 0x120 is only the highest strong field + 4.

fields.name: maybe_windowKind
fields.evidence: `if (*(char *)(param_1 + 0x11c) == '\x02')` in maybe_Ui_BuildFlags (0x0064055C): a u8 discriminator compared against 2 that selects the second flag byte; the R2_013 doc calls it the window kind. The callers pass the object returned by func_00213E30() (a text-argument source, see Ui_DiveWindow_SetTextArg4), so the owning class is not the result window.

summary: Save-slot window: owns the label record at +0x764 whose text is the slot name shown in the save menu.
evidence: The only method Ui_SaveWindow_LoadSlotName (0x0025C480) is a 0-byte tail call: wcslen(maybe_Ui_Window_GetLabelText(self+0x764)) followed by 0x001B7DDC, which wcsncpy's five characters into the slot-name field. The class name comes from that one function name, so the save-window identity is plausible but unproven. Size 1896 = 0x768 is only the highest strong field + 4.

fields.name: slotNameLabel
fields.evidence: `maybe_Ui_Window_GetLabelText(self + 0x764)` (0x0064A2C8) resolves the label text of the record at +0x764: it reads a data-manager record id at +4, an inline buffer at +0xC, flags at +0x1C..+0x1E, a kind at +0x20 and inline UTF-16 text at +0x22. So +0x764 is an embedded label record - not a Casino_Slot, which the stale structs.json type guess said (0x0064A2C8 used to be named maybe_Casino_Slot_EvaluateWinLines) - and its text is the save slot name.

A real one-pane window, but which screen uses it is not shown. Size 212 = 0xD4 is only the highest strong field + 4.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Vtable 0x0076A230 recovered from the pointer table; slot 0 is Ui_SinglePaneWindow_Dtor (0x003D627C) and slot 7 is the class init 0x003D6238, so the table belongs to this class. The store itself happens in the shared base constructor 0x001A6520, which is why struct_db has no offset-0 access for this class.

fields.name: unknown_0d0
